description: List the footnotes an article cites — its reference lists, in document order — with each footnote's text, external links (archive copies included), and DOIs. wikipedia_get_article drops footnote markers and reference lists, so use this for the sources behind a claim. label is the in-text marker without brackets; group names a notes list such as "lower-alpha" and is absent for the main list. A short citation such as "Galinsky 2012, pp. 75–76" carries work_ids, and works on the same page holds the full citations they name, each once. Pages hold whole footnotes within 40,000 UTF-8 bytes on both surfaces; follow next_cursor as cursor with the same title and language to continue at the same revision. Bibliography and further-reading entries no footnote points to are not listed — read those sections with wikipedia_get_article. Redirects are followed; the revision_id and url cite the article read.

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor from the previous page. Keep title and language unchanged. Empty means the first page.

title.description: Article title (e.g. "Seine"). A trailing #fragment is accepted and ignored; the characters < > [ ] { } and | cannot appear in a Wikipedia page name.

name: wikipedia_get_references

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `not_found`: No Wikipedia article exists for the given title, or the title is blank. `invalid_title`: The title contains characters MediaWiki cannot name a page with. `invalid_language`: The language is not a valid BCP 47 code, or names a Wikipedia edition that does not exist. `invalid_cursor`: The cursor is malformed, was issued for another title or language, or points past the last footnote. `revision_unavailable`: The revision the cursor is pinned to no longer exists, is hidden, or cannot be read or verified. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

next_cursor.description: Pass unchanged as cursor with the same title and language for the next page. Absent on the last page.

notice.description: Where to look instead when the article has no footnotes.

pageid.description: Wikipedia page ID. Absent on API parse responses that omit it.

redirected_from.description: Original alias followed to the resolved article.

references.description: Footnotes on this page, in document order. Empty when the article has none.

group.description: Notes group the footnote belongs to (e.g. "lower-alpha", "N"). Absent for the main reference list.

label.description: In-text marker without brackets (e.g. "2", "a", "N 1"). Absent when no marker in the article links to the footnote.

text.description: Footnote text as plain text. Markers of other footnotes inside it are kept as [label].

urls.description: Every external link in the footnote, verbatim, archive copies included.

work_ids.description: CITEREF anchors a short citation links to. The citations they name are in works on the same page.

revision_id.description: ID of the revision the footnotes were read from. Every page of one read carries the same revision.

total_references.description: Footnotes in the article across every reference list, on all pages.

url.description: Canonical desktop URL of the article (e.g. "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seine"), for citing the page.

works.description: Full citations the work_ids on this page resolve to, each once. A work_id with no matching anchor in the article has no entry.

id.description: CITEREF anchor id of the full citation (e.g. "CITEREFGalinsky2012").

urls.description: Every external link in the citation, verbatim, archive copies included.

title: Get Wikipedia References
